map_desc: A forest rich in diverse nature. It is said mages come here to gather medicinal herbs.
Grasslands surrounded by mountains. To the west lies the gateway to a dangerous desert.

first_visit_condition: Accepted: Legacy of a Legendary Sculptor

map_desc: A tranquil gorge. It's said a river flowed through it before Dagsion was built.
A pass on a dark, steep mountain road. The abundant bushes make visibility poor.
An open area deep in the valley that has endless winds. Plants of all kinds grow wild.
Plain cloaked in fog, making visibility difficult. It is home to a variety of creatures.
A pass on Carmenta Road near the imperial capital. It is thought to be fairly safe.
A hill with a pleasant breeze in all seasons, from which one can look upon Dagsion.
A fairly easy pass to walk, with views of Dagsion and Lake Baal.
A small clearing in the forest where warriors sometimes go to fight duels.
An enormous bridge built to the west of Dagsion, the imperial capital.
A massive bridge built to the east of Dagsion, the imperial capital.
A lake formed by overflow from Lake Baal, located along the Sobek River.
A large bridge over the Talto River. One of Amalthea's key transportation hubs.
A mansion by the southern shore of Lake Baal. It is in ruins and devoid of life.
An underground graveyard near Dagsion. Often compared to a city due to its size.
The remains of a fort that used to protect the roads, along with Xantha Stronghold.
Sprawling plains between the grasslands in central Dagda and the southern forests.
Once a guibouga forest before its trees were chopped down to build Dagdan warships.
A pass at the foot of Aurora's temple, beloved by astronomers as a stargazing spot.
This route's name comes from local lore that it makes travelers feel lighter.
The most expansive plains in Melias, in whose fertile grounds many fauna reside.
A battle was fought here centuries ago, and its dead are said to reappear in the fog.
A lake in a vast wetland that's also an excellent fishing destination.
A strange man-made slab that lies next to the Great Tartarus Ruins.
(NOTE: This spot seems to be cut/unused, it is not assigned)
(to any location on the map, meaning it is currently inaccessible)
Barrows built so the souls of the Mulciber Marshlands' fallen warriors can find repose.
A village abandoned by its inhabitants when its soils turned toxic.
An ancient underground structure whose ceiling collapsed, revealing it to the world.
The ruins of a fort built in a marshland. At one time, it was a bandit hideout.
A bridge between Melias and Elektra, previously fortified but now unmanned.
A path to Ahm Lu, the royal capital of Damascar, also known as the Pilgrim's Path.
A flower garden, said to have been created when a star fell long ago.
Dense woods in the south of Saramis. Home to peoples of the forest.
A pass known by people in the area as a perfect spot to view the moon.
A great tree on the edge of Faun's Forest that many view as an object of worship.
The highest peak in Northern Dagda, with a summit covered in snow year-round.
A natural fortress of sorts, with a labyrinthine layout of steep rock walls.
A large valley by the Saramis Thoroughfare. It runs alongside a mountain stream.
A beautiful lake in Cybele, which holds huge quantities of water.

first_visit_condition: Accepted: Legacy of a Legendary Sculptor

map_desc: A beautiful, sandy shore, from which an ominous island is visible in the distance.
A cemetery hidden in the forest, lined with ancient Damascarine gravestones.
A place where it's said that one can converse with the spirits of the forest.
A lighthouse next to the capital city Megaira that guides ships on the Danann Sea.
When the wind blows through these woods' broad-leaved trees, a wailing sound is made.
A place that nearby peoples use as a communal burial ground.
A large rock marking ancient execution grounds, so locals are fearful of it.
Ruins left by the ancient Djilu kingdom, a casualty of the Mosa's aggression.
A castle once held by the Mosa, since renovated by Saramis into a great fortress.
Surrounding terrain blocks this pass from sunlight, leaving it in constant darkness.
A glade in the forest where a weighty silence hangs over everything.
A rock reminiscent of a smiling old man's face. Travelers use it as a landmark.
Sand dunes in the outer edge of the desert. The grasses may spontaneously combust.
Ruins of an altar where Yu Phas is said to have purified herself for her wedding.
A hollow that suddenly opened in the forest. It has a diverse variety of plants.
Mountains at the desert's edge, from which the forbidden land's walls can be seen.
A plateau in the grasslands where a terrible incident occurred in ancient times.
A lake filled with salty waters that are decidedly not potable.
A large freshwater lake in Lambath. Jurah's temple reflects on its surface.
A stunning and otherworldly arrangement of rocks carved out by water erosion.
Those who get lost in the desert might make it out through here—if they're lucky.
The remains of an ancient fort that travelers had used as a landmark to reach the oasis.
A rugged path where the brave champion Breza trained in his youth.
A steep mountain path taken by temple ascetics going to the summit.
The final destination of those who can no longer endure training on Mount Orgus.
A hill where, according to legend, a group of giants once lived.
A mountain road that warriors from Brezarant take to scale Mount Orgus.
A valley that appears in tales of the lands' giants, said to have been torn open by a fist.
A lake with clean, pure waters, originating from Naimi Lake.
Shallow caves that glow in a deep-green color. There are high-quality ores within.
A small tower that was once the home of a reclusive mage.
A ghost town whose inhabitants abandoned it after a Demonic Beast attack.
The road leading to Credna's temple next to a deep forest stretching to the south.
A place with numerous gravestones. Ancient warriors were laid to rest here.
A mountain range looming over a large forest, said to have been raised by giants.
A forest with a trade route in it. Those who stray are often attacked by beasts.
An animal trail that's easy to get lost on, so the locals are wary of taking it.
A small waterfall. Legend has it that visitors can hear prophecies from a gorgeous spirit.
Though this place hosts useful minerals, few visit as it is so far from the town.
Ruins, the age and purpose of which are unknown. They are shaped like a tower.
The ruins of a legendary giants' fort, it was also a battlefield in the Zodiac Incident.
A mountain pass leading to Kalla's temple taken by many performers and merchants.
A mountainous region composing most of Cydonia. A road was cut through it.
A pass on the road in northern Arago that watches over many travelers.
A gap in the rocks near the eroded valley by a trade route. One person can fit through.
A huge lake on the slopes of the Ere Mountains that hosts unique species of fish.
A small salt field, salt from which is consumed in the kingdom of Arago.
The vault where the kingdom of Arago stocks supplies in case of crisis.

first_visit_condition: Accepted: A Letter of Some Gravity / For the Empire's Safety

map_desc: The tomb of Cohen, the legendary bard. Its structure is often compared to a gallery's.
A fort built to defend the eastern territories of the kingdom of Arago.
Remains of a checkpoint built in antiquity, glaring at the desert's exit.
A trade route at the edge of the desert, known to lead travelers astray.
A valley made famous in the legend of Arago, blanketed in thick miasma.
A cape in the desert. Humid winds blowing in from the sea lead to diverse plant growth.
A giant rock. Prophecy says this is where the Herald of the Pale Raven will appear.
A gorge at the foot of the Mountain of Fire, echoing with the howls of Demonic Beasts.
A huge outcrop that bears a similar appearance to a gateway.
The highest peak in the Iapetus Mountains. It is where many legends are set.
Unique, geometric, natural rock formations the likes of which can only be seen here.
A valley filled with poisonous gases from the volcano. Passing through can be fatal.
The gases coming from the Mountain of Fire makes it dangerous to mine its minerals.
A fortress built to guard the road to the Iapetus Mountains.
The remains of a settlement abandoned long ago, seemingly due to pollution in the river.
A sand dune a little ways from the desert, famous for its excellent view.
A lake of the dead with clear, blue, highly acidic water. It is unsurvivable for fish.
A ceremonial altar that was once in the outskirts, since burned down.
A plain near Solel's temple, named for the Sunbearer himself.
A pass on a slight slope named for Solel, the Sunbearer.
A hilly area on Amalthea's border where one can enjoy magnificent views.
A vast plateau seated within the relatively fertile, hilly lands of Elektra.
One of a trio of rocks. Its blessings are said to facilitate amicable partings.
One of a trio of rocks. Its blessings are said to preserve and strengthen love.
One of a trio of rocks. Its blessings are said to create new opportunities for connection.
A mountain path dappled by sunlight filtering through the broad-leaved trees.
A garden cast in soft sunlight, on a plain between the mountains.
A cape overlooking the Danann Sea. It is famed for its striking views.
An abandoned fort that was once a beautiful sight when lit by the setting sun.
A temple dedicated to Solel, the Sunbearer. It is currently not in use.

first_visit_condition: Accepted: Legacy of a Legendary Sculptor

map_desc: Though usually unmanned, it would be used to defend Elektra in an emergency.
A mountain thought to be sacred due to its otherworldly beauty.
A back road passing through the mountains, rumored to pass by some mysterious ruins.
A cape with towering rock cliffs that has bau flying over it.
Vast plains not far from the notorious Bran Narrows.
A deep valley that rejects human intrusion, home to many species of pegasus.
A cave where many useful minerals can be mined, visited by many fortune seekers.
The remains of a ship that was stranded at Bran Narrows. Its origins are unclear.
A cape at the tip of the peninsula where debris from the Lir Sea often washes up.
A formation resembling an open mouth; waves lap in and out like it's telling secrets.
A pass on a highway in the mountains. The view is poor, and bandits abound.

first_visit_condition: Accepted: Legacy of a Legendary Sculptor

map_desc: The largest waterfall in Castalia. Legend has it that behind it lies hidden treasure.
A pass on the road that runs along the rugged Veletta Range.
A garden planted to celebrate a visit from the legendary bard Cohen.
A somewhat open area in the forest that leads to the cape.
A huge rock shaped like a pegasus. Beyond the sea here lies the vast land of Banbha.
A forest made whitish by accumulated elements from the surrounding area.
A pass at a fork in the road, rumored to lead to secret hot springs.
A reef near the fishing village of Fina, home to a variety of creatures.
A den where numerous squirming swarms of insects thrive.
It is not known when this pit was dug, but it is said to have a hot spring at the bottom.
Many people get caught in quicksand here. The farther west, the stronger its pull.
A rocky spread of ruins that dates back to before the empire's founding.
A rock ledge where the desert's sandworms come to lay their eggs.
A relatively safe spot at the edge of the desert where various plants grow.
The end point of a huge flow of quicksand. Those who go in do not come out.
The entrance to a notoriously treacherous desert.
A plain in the desert where one of the most famed battles in imperial history took place.
A junction in the northern Tarvos plains. Beyond it, sand stretches to the horizon.
A junction in the southern Tarvos plains. Beyond it, sand stretches to the horizon.
The remains of an ancient battlefield. Huge, decayed metal pillars stand like graves.
A pit formed in the quicksand. Anyone who gets sucked in will not come out alive.
Ruins of the capital of Iskandariya, which flourished in ancient times.
Built long ago to monitor seas to the west, now left uninhabited.
A huge bay at the mouth of the Talto River. It has few waves and excellent fishing.
A junction of currents in the Lir Sea, all flowing in fixed directions.
Waters where the Pasha Currents change into a more complex flow.
Waters haunted by large sharks. Some report seeing them fight sea beasts.
The collision of currents here created a whirlpool that wanders like a lost child.
A place off the coast of Niiza Port with two rock pillars that resemble a massive gate.
A sea passage near Fódlan, just next to Eif.
A fishing ground that supplies the Port of Pandora with the bounties of the Lir Sea.
Waters near the Adrestian Empire in Fódlan. Shipwrecks are frequent.
An area with shoals and striking coral reefs. Large ships must take caution here.
A perilous strait lying between Dagda and the foreign land of Banbha.
Though there's a visible entrance on the seafloor, it's seemingly impossible to enter.
A gate-like rock formation, said to be the entrance to the former kingdom of Solomon.
An uninhabited oasis where a diverse range of plants thrive.
An anomalous cave that has ores found in the sea despite being in a desert.
Due to strong winds in the area, it takes veteran sailors to make landfall here.
A tower made known to locals through tales and legends, supposedly never reached.
The island where Balor supposedly slumbers. Also called the Isle of Sorrows.
A small island off the coast of Saramis, inhabited by many skilled fishers.
This bay, a bountiful fishing ground, is considered the gateway to Dagsion.
A sea region outlying Peluza Cape, where many of Danann's pirates reside.
Waters feared by merchants due to the presence of rapacious pirates.
Tranquil coastal waters near Aonghas Strait, just north of a treacherous reef.
This fishing ground hosts numerous ships, from nearby settlements as well as Megaira.
The unusual terrain and conditions in this area foment many small whirlpools.
A perilous spot in the Danann Circulation Corridor. One wrong move, your ship sinks.
A walled village in the forbidden land where the People of the White Egg live.
